rationale: On the 84.4% of 2025 closing quotes that are within 10 cents -- the ones a trader could actually cross -- player props are overpriced on the YES side in five adjacent price buckets, monotonically increasing with price: -0.0147 at 0.20-0.35, -0.0284 at 0.35-0.50, -0.0485 at 0.50-0.65, -0.0380 at 0.65-0.80, -0.0412 at 0.80-0.90, on 199 games with game-clustered standard errors. Spreads and totals over the same books are flat to within about one standard error at every bucket. This replaced two earlier findings (H-016 and a receptions underpricing) that were artefacts of untradable books.
features: closing midpoint bucket restricted to books quoted within 10 cents, family, game-clustered
target: realised settlement rate minus closing midpoint on player props, and NO-side net return after the Kalshi taker fee
expected_direction: The YES-side overpricing persists on 2026 settled props at roughly 2-5 points and remains monotone in price. The NO-side net return after fees stays at or below zero: on 2025 it pooled to -0.0126 +- 0.0104, best single bucket +0.0044 +- 0.0147.
test_plan: Prospective on 2026 settled player props, plus a re-run on the remaining 46% of the 2025 backfill. All calibration restricted to books within 10 cents. Pre-specified primary endpoint: pooled bias across buckets at or above 0.20. Co-equal secondary: pooled NO-side net return after fees, with a clustered SE excluding zero required before any tradability claim. Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10.
result: 2025 at 54% coverage, tradable books: five buckets all negative, three at 2.4-3.3 SE, 199 games. NO-side pooled net -0.0126 +- 0.0104.
notes: The direction agrees with the shadow model, which prices props about 0.019 below the market after the availability haircut (H-011): on tradable 2025 books the market did settle below its own quotes. Whether 0.019 is the right magnitude is open. Registered with tradability as a co-equal endpoint for the same reason H-016 was, and H-016 is why that matters.
